summary: Iteration 16 — frontend-only verification of the new EPG on-screen progress/status bar (src/components/EpgProgressBar.tsx) wired via store.tsx (subscribeProgress → epgProgress → useStore) and rendered under the chip row in app/(tabs)/index.tsx. Tested at mobile viewport 390x844 on https://iptv-player-guide.preview.emergentagent.com. RESULTS — ALL 7 REVIEW ITEMS PASS. (1) Guide surface loaded at t=0.24s; EPG program cells reached 865 within ~7s, well under the 15s SLA; UI stayed responsive during the parse. (2) EPG-BAR (testID 'epg-progress-bar') appeared at t≈2.4s with label 'Downloading TV guide… 0%' (web fetch has no byte-progress so it briefly shows 0% — matches the review note), then transitioned to 'Building TV guide… 30% → 34% → 45% → 69% → 90%' with ETA text '~1s left' as parsing progressed, and auto-hid at t=6.94s once 865 program cells were in the DOM. Both `phase='downloading'` and `phase='parsing'` labels were observed; percentage climbed monotonically 0→90+ and the Animated fill width tracked the ratio. (3) ProgramModal opens on tapping epg-prog-* cell (verified with epg-prog-'AMC.us (m3u4u)-0'); program-watch-btn AND program-modal-close both present; close-btn dismisses modal; Watch navigates to /player without crash. (4) Box grid (mode-box-btn → epg-box-grid) and Timeline (mode-timeline-btn → epg-timeline-grid) both render; az-rail is present in BOTH modes. Progress bar is rendered ABOVE the grid area (under chip row) so it is visible in box mode too. (5) chip-All / chip-Favorites filter without regression; guide-refresh-btn works (does NOT re-trigger the progress bar because refresh() re-slices the in-memory guide within TTL — bar only reappears when an actual re-fetch happens; this matches the 'may reappear' language in the review). (6) Favorites, Search, Settings tabs all render and route. (7) Console/pageerrors: 0 uncaught JS errors, 0 non-benign warnings.
action_items: None required for correctness — all 7 review items pass on the web preview and no regressions were introduced by the store.epgProgress addition or the new EpgProgressBar component.

Optional (nice-to-have, non-blocking): guide-refresh-btn currently calls refresh() which re-slices the in-memory guide within TTL and does NOT trigger the progress bar. Since hardRefresh() (bound to pull-to-refresh) already forces a re-fetch, this is acceptable; but if the intent is 'tapping refresh should always show the progress bar again', wire the header refresh button to hardRefresh (or expose a 'force' path that resets the progress phase to 'downloading').

Native-only validation (out of web preview scope, per the review note): (a) confirm on a real Android TV box that the new FileSystem.createDownloadResumable → base64 → fflate.gunzip path actually downloads the ~2.5 MB gzipped /epg/ payload and unpacks it (log the downloaded byte count vs totalBytesExpectedToWrite); (b) confirm the progress bar shows a climbing % during the DOWNLOAD phase (native has real byte-progress via onDownload callback — web does not), then a climbing % during the PARSE phase; (c) confirm the bar auto-hides once phase='ready'.
critical_code_review_comments: src/source.ts fetchEpgBytes — native path is correct: createDownloadResumable emits onDownload with totalBytesWritten/totalBytesExpectedToWrite (may be 0 on chunked servers → null ratio → bar stays at 0% until parse, which is exactly what the label 'Downloading TV guide…' + null ETA conveys). Web path continues to use fetch().arrayBuffer() through the /api/proxy so the existing CORS-safe flow is preserved. The temp file is deleted after read (idempotent) — no cache leak. Good.

src/source.ts progress model — download is bucketed to 0..0.3 and parse to 0.3..1.0 of the overall EPG step, so the bar makes visual sense end-to-end. setProgress throttles emits to 150ms except on 'force' transitions (initial, ready, error), which is exactly the right balance for a status bar (avoids re-render storms while feeling live). ETA math is guarded by ratio>0.02 && elapsed>0.5 so we never show a nonsense ETA at the start. Verified in the UI as '~1s left' during parse.

src/source.ts subscribeProgress — new subscription immediately invokes fn(progress) so the store gets the current snapshot on mount, preventing a stale/empty first render. Cleanup via filter is correct.

src/store.tsx — adds epgProgress state initialized to {phase:'idle', ratio:0, etaSeconds:null}, subscribes via useEffect(() => subscribeProgress(setEpgProgress), []) which returns the unsub function so it's properly cleaned up on unmount. The context value now includes epgProgress; no other consumer had to change. Clean minimal API surface.

src/components/EpgProgressBar.tsx — visibility gate is correct: renders during 'channels' | 'downloading' | 'parsing' | 'error', hidden on 'idle' and 'ready'. Animated width uses useNativeDriver:false (required for layout property width — correct). Min bar width clamped to 3% so users see something even at 0%. ETA formatter handles sub-60s and >60s cases; guards NaN/negative/infinite. Uses View/Text/Animated (RN primitives). No hard-coded colors.

app/(tabs)/index.tsx — EpgProgressBar placed BETWEEN chipRowWrap and the grid conditional, so (a) it never overlaps the ScrollView chips (which have their own fixed height wrap), (b) it appears in both timeline AND box modes, and (c) it disappears once loading transitions to 'ready' without shifting the grid on mount (initial gap is small: paddingBottom:sm + 6 gap). No layout jank observed on mode toggle.

success_rate.frontend: 7/7 review-request items verified passing on the web preview

context_for_next_testing_agent: Base URL: https://iptv-player-guide.preview.emergentagent.com. Mobile viewport 390x844. New testID: 'epg-progress-bar' (single element, inner_text is 'Downloading TV guide…\n<pct>%' or 'Building TV guide…\n<pct>%  ·  ~<n>s left' or 'Guide unavailable — showing channels only' on error). Bar is only visible during phases channels/downloading/parsing/error — hidden on idle/ready. On the WEB preview, download phase shows only 0% (fetch has no byte-progress); parse phase shows a climbing % with ETA. Observed timing on web: bar appears ~2.4s, parse label appears ~5.5s, bar hidden ~7s with 865 program cells rendered. guide-refresh-btn calls refresh() (in-memory re-slice) NOT hardRefresh(), so it does NOT reappear the bar within TTL — this is by design. All other testIDs from iteration_15 unchanged.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no regressions. The new epgProgress channel in the store (added lines 62/88-92/156 in store.tsx) is a pure additive subscription (subscribeProgress → setEpgProgress) and does not alter any existing behavior. The new EpgProgressBar renders null when phase is idle/ready so it has zero layout footprint outside the active loading window. The source.ts progress emit path uses a 150ms throttle so it cannot flood React re-renders.
